title: ARTS & CRAFTS ENGLISH OAK PEG ...
reason: Solid pegged oak trestle coffee table in a sought-after Arts and Crafts style; attribution and age unproven and unmarked, so a modest candidate.
findings: Two photos. Low rectangular trestle coffee table with a plank top and moulded edge, two shaped trestle ends (pierced waist) each with a cross-shaped key peg through the tenon, a plinth foot at each end and a rail or stretcher underneath. The pegged joints and chunky shapes fit the 'peg and dowel Arts and Crafts' description, but similar pieces were made well into the 1930s to 1950s, so age cannot be pinned down. The top looks light and plain, and the grain is not clearly oak in the photos. No maker's label, stamp or brand seen; the underside and stretcher are not photographed. Small white stock stickers on the top (not maker's marks).
condition: Light surface wear: faint scratches and small marks on the top with a slightly bleached centre and mild edge wear; joints look tight and no obvious damage.
rescore_note: Solid pegged trestle coffee table in a common style; age could be anywhere from the 1920s to 1950s, grain not clearly oak, no maker mark and the underside is unseen, so low-value furniture around the $30-80 to $80-200 border. Estimate only, no live comps.
